messages:
emma: FYI I'm seeing linkcheck flake on docs-CI. Only fails in the parallel matrix jobs with a 404 for /guides/compat/include-snippet.html

mika: Hmm, seen that before. Any failing logs?

emma: copied the relevant line from the job:
linkcheck-bot: [linkcheck] ERROR 404: GET https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/compat/include-snippet.html

emma: Our site uses include-markdown + mkdocs-macros-plugin. I suspect a race where the included artifact isn't present yet in the parallel runner.

samir: CI generates shared includes in a prior step and uploads them as artifacts. The matrix jobs then download and run mkdocs in parallel — could be an ordering issue.

mika: Can you paste the include syntax from the source page?

emma: sure, it's simple:
```
{! ../shared/includes/compat-overview.md !}
```

ria: That's the include-markdown pattern. If the file isn't present or the redirect generator hasn't run, linkcheck sees the final output missing and flags 404.

mika: My hunch: redirect generator (post-build) creates convenience HTMLs and sometimes linkcheck runs before those redirect files are produced when jobs run concurrently.

samir: I could repro locally by spinning two builds in parallel while the generate_redirects script runs. Running `MKDOCS_ENV=ci python scripts/generate_redirects.py && mkdocs build --clean` serially avoids the flake.

emma: Short-term workaround: make the linkcheck job depend on the artifact step or sequence the redirect generation before linkcheck.

mika: Opening a quick PR to add an explicit `needs: build-artifacts` to the linkcheck matrix job so it runs after uploads are available: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/5123

emma: Awesome. Can we also add a note to CONTRIBUTING.md about ordering when working with includes so future PRs avoid this?

samir: Done — added a one-liner and a minimal backoff in the artifact publisher to reduce race windows (:grimacing:).

mika: Ran CI on my fork with the ordering change — linkcheck now stable. Will merge once org CI is green.

ci-bot: Build passed — linkcheck job succeeded in matrix 3/3 :white_check_mark:

emma: Thanks all! I'll follow up with a tiny docs cleanup PR to replace a couple of risky `{! ... !}` includes with explicit relative files in high-traffic pages.

mika: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.
